name: NASA International Space Apps Challenge
organizer: NASA Space Apps Global Organizing Team (funded by NASA's Earth Science Division)
venue: 485 in-person and virtual Local Events plus the virtual Universal Event

tracks.name: Create an Orrery Web App that Displays Near-Earth Objects
Leveraging Earth Observation Data for Informed Agricultural Decision-Making
Seismic Detection Across the Solar System
Landsat Reflectance Data: On the Fly and at Your Fingertips
Navigator for the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO): Mapping the Characterizable Exoplanets in our Galaxy

prizes.name: Best Use of Science
prizes.definition: The best and most valid use of science and/or the scientific method.

prizes.name: Best Use of Data
prizes.definition: Best makes space data accessible or leverages it for a unique application.

prizes.name: Best Use of Technology
prizes.definition: The most innovative use of technology.

prizes.name: Galactic Impact
prizes.definition: The most potential to improve life on Earth or in the universe.

prizes.name: Best Mission Concept
prizes.definition: The most plausible concept and design.

prizes.name: Most Inspirational
prizes.definition: The project that captures our hearts.

prizes.name: Best Storytelling
prizes.definition: Most creatively communicates the potential of open data through the art of storytelling.

prizes.name: Global Connection
prizes.definition: Best connects people around the world through technology.

prizes.name: Art & Technology
prizes.definition: Most effectively combines technical and creative skills.

prizes.name: Local Impact
prizes.definition: The greatest potential for local impact.

criteria.label: Influence
criteria.description: How much good the project can do, in quality and quantity. Renamed 'Impact' in 2025.

criteria.label: Creativity
criteria.description: How novel the approach is, versus an incremental improvement on something that exists.

criteria.label: Validity
criteria.description: Scientifically valid; does what it sets out to do; can work in the real world.

criteria.label: Relevance
criteria.description: Responsive to the chosen challenge; complete; technically feasible; usable.

criteria.label: Presentation
criteria.description: How well the team tells the story: the challenge, the proposed solution and why it matters.

judging.judge_profile_summary: Three phases. Local and Universal Event judges choose Global Nominees (940+); NASA and Space Agency Partner subject-matter experts choose 40 Global Finalists plus Honorable Mentions; an executive committee of agency leaders assigns the 10 Global Awards.
judging.notes: Criteria from the 2024 Judging & Awards guide (third-party-hosted copy); each is scored 1–5.

required_tech: At least one NASA data source or resource
submission_requirements: Project page on spaceappschallenge.org with summary, demonstration link, project link, details, use of AI, NASA data and other data
Use and link at least one NASA data source or resource
1–6 members registered for the same Local Event or the Universal Event
'Create Your Own Challenge' projects are not eligible for global judging

organizer_takeaways.claim: The 10 Global Winners were chosen from 40 Global Finalists, who were selected from 940+ Global Nominees out of 9,996 submissions.

sources.note: 10 Global Winners with award, challenge, city/country and description; 93,520 registered participants, 485 events, 163 countries, 9,996 submissions.
